title: The story planet ships baked: relaxed vertices and carve read back in 0.7 s instead of built in 5 s
context: Owner: the story mode always takes several seconds to load; check how heavy it is and what can be optimized. Measured: buildStoryPlanet 9 s in Node (relax 4.1 s, generateDungeon 4.4 s, of which buildCellGraph is 0.1 s) and about 5 s in Chrome on every load; downloads 27 MB at stage 7, 26 MB of it landmark models (solar complex 9.2 MB, Terraformer 4.1 MB, HUGIN pad 3.2 MB, diorama 2.1 MB, rocket 1.6 MB).
outcome: src/core/planet-bake.js encodes and decodes a bake (header with the recipe key, float32 vertices, uint8 tags, uint16 distances, heart, spawn, seeds); scripts/bake-planet.mjs (npm run bake) writes assets/story/planet.bin (1.07 MB). buildStoryPlanet takes an optional bake and, when its key and counts match, reads the vertices and the carve back and rebuilds only the lattice and the cell graph with the kernel's own array types. src/platform/planet-bake.js fetches it once; main.js awaits it before the story routes; the lab uses it too. test/planet-bake.mjs proves the bake reproduces a live build (same carve, heart, spawn, seeds, distances, clearing, mouth, lattice; vertices within 1e-6) and refuses other recipes. Chrome: lab build 5.0 s -> 0.7 s; the game reaches ready in 2.2 s at stage 7. The stage strip in the menu now reads STAGES (it had lost the tank bay).
alternatives: IndexedDB cache of the live build: rejected, the first load on every device still pays the 5 s.
A Web Worker: rejected, it moves the wait off the main thread but does not shorten it.
Quantised int16 vertices (0.4 MB): rejected for now, float32 keeps the bake provably equal to the live build.
evidence: node test/planet-bake.mjs: 806 ms baked vs 8805 ms live, identical carve
npm test 92, npm run check (49 pure-layer modules)
node scripts/browser-test.mjs --story-world and --story PASS; lab status reads built in 0.7 s
